emma.devex: quick check — mobile SDK (kotlin) getting SSE with partial JSON chunks, multibyte utf8 split, and token-refresh reconnects. seen lots of malformed json errors when we try to parse per-chunk. anyone have a resilient reassembly pattern? also worried about backpressure spikes when app comes from bg and k/v cache miss.

nate-runtime: we've seen this. usual pattern: accumulate bytes in a buffer, attempt incremental parse, only drop consumed bytes on success. for sse use event-level delim (\n\n) when possible. for partial json inside event, try a streaming json decoder rather than `JSON.parse` on each chunk.

sophia-client: for JS/native-mobile we use TextDecoder and keep leftover string. pseudocode:
```
buffer += decoder.decode(chunk, {stream: true})
while (true) {
  const idx = buffer.indexOf('\n\n')
  if (idx === -1) break
  const event = buffer.slice(0, idx)
  buffer = buffer.slice(idx + 2)
  try { handle(JSON.parse(event)) } catch(e) { // put event back + wait }
}
```
worked for us with multibyte splits.

liam-go: in go `json.Decoder` on an io.Reader is simpler. But if you're doing raw byte frames, do `bytes.Buffer` + `json.Decoder` with `UseNumber()` and check `io.EOF` vs `io.ErrUnexpectedEOF`. Also watch goroutine spawn on reconnects — add rate limiter/backoff to avoid burst reconnects when tokens bounce.

amanda-py: python client edge case: `json.JSONDecodeError` often means partial. we do `buf += chunk.decode('utf-8', errors='replace')` then try `json.loads` in a loop, but prefer `orjson` or `ijson` for incremental. for backpressure we expose `max_buffer_bytes` and drop events older than X or pause upstream.

emma.devex: thanks — curious about auth-refresh race: token refresh triggers reconnect which replays same stream from start causing duplicates. how to dedupe/seek safely?

nate-runtime: prefer idempotent events with event ids from server. if impossible, client should track last seen event id and skip until > last. server should support `Last-Event-ID` header or resume cursor.

sophia-client: if server doesn't expose ids, use a sliding hash window of recent payloads to dedupe, but memory heavy. also add jittered backoff on token-refresh so not everyone reconnects at same ms.

liam-go: for mobile specifically, when app resumes, throttle reconnect to 1 per 2s and let runtime coalesce. also lower initial concurrency while warmup to avoid backpressure.

deploy-bot: staging deploy succeeded 1848001400 — monitoring for increased reconnects.

emma.devex: great. i'll open a tiny PR adding reassembly helpers in kotlin and link to this thread. thanks all :thumbsup:
